- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–3% to forecast if sentiment >0.7 and price >70.
- If model forecast is >75% above recent 18-day average, apply mean reversion correction: reduce by 10–15% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price increases; add 1–2% to forecast if sentiment >0.5 and price >70 in last 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive low sentiment), model tends to ignore sentiment; force a 5–10% downward adjustment to forecast.
